Entry point of the game proper (the loader's jump at $9548 runs the start-up at $95xx, which falls into here). Sets the CIA2 VIC bank, switches sprites 0 and 1 on with sprite 2 and 3 colours, copies 17 bytes of initial sprite registers from $15EA, builds the opening screen with $0B3B and falls into the main loop.

Top of the main loop. Runs once per pass: it first checks whether the energy or clock has run out (the flag at $0206), then whether Johnny has walked far enough right to leave the room, then does the per-frame work (scroll, input, messages, mode handler) and loops back here.

Not out of energy: tests whether the scroll position has reached the room's exit column ($FC) with the sprite inside the exit area and the right screen set; if so the room is left, otherwise it carries on to the scroll and sprite update below.

Per-frame body of the main loop: if the frame flag at $02BE is clear it only runs $0580 and loops; otherwise it clears the flag, checks for a scroll step, runs the per-pass subsystems in turn (energy and timer checks, input, jump, messages, enemies) and finally dispatches to the handler for the current mode through the table at $43E8, or to the action handler when fire is pressed in mode 0.
Idle branch of the main loop: runs the keyboard/action poll at $203A and goes back to the top of the loop.
Turns the joystick state in $20 into edge flags: fire held ($0201), fire pressed this pass ($0202), direction held ($0203) and direction pressed this pass ($0204).
Clears the fire edge flag and falls into the direction flags.
Moves Johnny's two sprites up one pixel, or does nothing at the top limit ($40), and updates the scroll flag; one of the four per-direction steps the walk code calls through the table at $1C2E.
Moves Johnny's two sprites down one pixel (limit tested in the caller), part of the per-direction walk steps.
Moves Johnny's sprites left one pixel unless he is at X $84; if he is at the left limit it sets the scroll direction to left ($FF) instead.

Moves the player sprite pair one pixel to the right when it is left of $E0 (setting the scroll direction to right); at the right edge it either stops (clears a flag) or asks the scroller to start moving.

Sets up the raster interrupt system: sets the time-of-day clock to 3:00, disables the CIA interrupts, enables the raster interrupt, points the IRQ vector at $0738 and starts the three-handler chain.

Part one's raster handler for the band that starts at line $A3, where the status panel begins (the previous handler set that line). Selects screen 0 and the character set, sets the multicolour colours and the fixed horizontal scroll $18, sets the next interrupt line to $F3, raises the frame flag at $02BE, types the next message character when $0294 is set, and then runs the scroll step if one is wanted.
Common tail of the raster handlers: when the scroll direction $21 is non-zero it runs the scroll step $087B and sets $02BF to 1, then restores X, Y and A and returns.

Part one's raster handler for line $F3, below the panel. It sets the screen, colours and scroll register ($D016 from $22, $D011 from $02A1) that the next frame's playfield will use, sets the next interrupt for line 0, counts the frame counter $0306 up, runs the sound driver and, unless the pause flag $0217 is set, updates the clock.

Writes the four characters of one big clock digit (digit in A, position in Y) into the panel.
Part one's raster handler for line 0: only sets the next interrupt line to $A3.
Sets the CIA1 time-of-day clock to X hours and Y minutes, zero seconds and tenths, and redraws it.

Scrolls the playfield by two pixels in the direction given by the sign of $21 (negative is left): moves sprites 2 and 3, adjusts $22 (the horizontal scroll value) and, when it wraps, shifts the whole 40-column character map and colour map by one column.
Shifts every row of the character and colour maps one cell to the left (each row is 40 cells, 12 rows of each map), then goes to the column refill at $0A33.
Shifts every row of the character and colour maps one cell to the right (12 rows of each map), then goes to the column refill at $0A33.
After a scroll the new edge column is filled from the room's tile map: chooses the tile column to draw by the scroll phase and calls the tile draw at $0A92 and the column write at $0B00.
Fetches the three tile numbers of one map column from the room map tables at $4000, $4100 and $4200 (indexed by X) and stores their character data in the temporary column buffer at $02AF.
Looks up one tile's 16 characters (a 4 by 4 block at $5000 plus 16 times the tile number) and copies one column of four of them to the column buffer at $02AF.
Converts a tile number in A to its character data address: $5000 plus 16 times the number, in zero page $24/$25.
Writes the twelve characters in the column buffer to the screen map at $C050 and the matching colours (looked up from the table at $8448) to the colour copy at $D850, one column of the playfield.

Redraws the whole playfield from the room's tile map, starting at the current scroll column: for each of the 10 tile columns and 3 tile rows it expands the tile's characters into the screen map at $C050.

Second half of $0B3B: sets the scroll phase to $FF and fills the colour map at $D850 from the screen map at $C050, looking each character up in the colour table at $8448 (it reads each character with the undocumented opcode LAX, which loads A and X together).
Three screen-map pointers, $C050, $C0F0 and $C190: the start of each of the three tile rows of the playfield.
Three pointers, $4000, $4100 and $4200, to the three rows of part one's map; $0B3B reads them.
Data at $0BF1 (f_0BF1): read by build_screen.

Handler for the SEARCH action (entry 2 of the table at $0675, run when fire is pressed). Does nothing unless mode 0 is active and no message is queued; otherwise finds what is at the player's position with $0D62, and unless the player is too low queues message 0 (EXAMINE) and message 11 (PROCESSING), sets a delay of 100 passes and starts mode 1.

Second half of the mode 1 handler (search in progress): counts the delay at $02D4 down; at zero it reports the result: a locked container ($0DCA) gives LOCKED and ABORT, nothing found gives FOUND NOTHING and clears the mode, otherwise it queues FOUND and the name of each object found and moves to mode 2.
Sets the mode ($0200) to 0 and queues message 10, the prompt arrow.
Queues message 10, the prompt arrow, and returns.
Computes the map column under Johnny from sprite 0's X position, the scroll phase and the scroll column, and stores it in $021B.

Looks up what is at the player's map column: checks the tile at that column against the table at $153D, then the object table at $1568, collecting each matching object's number into the list at $02D7 and its name into $02DB; the count goes in $02D6 (negative if the player is too low).
Tests whether the container at the player's column is one that needs a key ($15BC), and whether its open flag in $020B is set; returns the carry set if it is still shut.
Queues the message number in A (without adding an offset).
Queues system message A, adding $0B so that 0 is PROCESSING (message 11).
Queues the object name for object number A, adding $35 to reach its text (object 0 is LASER ROM, message 53).
Queues the description message A, adding $4B to reach its text (description 0 is message 75).
Appends the message number in A to the message queue at $02C4 and bumps the queue length.
Starts printing the message at the head of the queue: finds its text in the message table at $0EBF by counting '!' terminators, and resets the print position.
Per-pass message printer: if nothing is printing it starts the next queued message; otherwise every third pass it types one more character, handling the control characters (newline, pause, end).
Ends the current message: shifts the queue down one entry, clears the printing flag and clears the window, unless the message was the blank prompt.

Game text, messages 0 to 52, each ended by '!' ($21). Letters are A to Z as 1 to 26, '2' is a line break, '3' is a short pause marker, digits and space are as ASCII. Messages 0 to 9 are the action menu words, 10 is the prompt arrow, 11 onwards the system messages, 48 to 52 the endings and part headings.
Continues text_messages ($0EBF to $12A0) at offset 321: Game text, messages 0 to 52, each ended by '!' ($21). No instruction names this address, the data is reached through an index or pointer.
Messages 53 to 88: the names of the 21 objects (53 to 73), a blank (74), and the descriptions (75 to 88) shown by DESCRIBE, each ended by '!'.
The 43 tile numbers that SEARCH accepts as something to search: $0D62 compares the tile in the room's middle row at the player's column with these.

The 21 objects, four bytes each: map column, layer (3 for the floor), object number and description number. Taking an object zeroes its column and layer; hiding one writes the container's column and layer back.
Data at $1569 (f_1569): written by mode_search_finish, mode_hide_do, reset_game_state; read by find_objects_here.
Data at $156A (f_156A): read by find_objects_here.
Data at $156B (f_156B): read by find_objects_here.
Data at $15A8 (a_15A8): read by check_laser_pickup.
Data at $15B8 (a_15B8): read by read_tenths.
The eight map columns that hold a locked container (drawer or cabinet), in the order of their bits in $15C4.
One bit per container, 1 to 128, for the open and key flags at $020B and $020C.
Ten three-byte entries (map column, then the address minus one of its INPUT handler): the places where an object can be used with INPUT.
Data at $15CD (f_15CD): read by mode_input_do.
Data at $15CE (f_15CE): read by mode_input_do.
Seventeen start values copied to the VIC registers $D000 to $D010 at game start: the sprite positions and the high bits.
Adds the three bytes at $02EA, $02EB and $02EC to the 6-digit decimal score at $02E7 to $02E9 (decimal mode), then redraws the score digits.
Draws the three score bytes at $02E7 to $02E9 as six big digits into the panel's score box.
Draws one score byte as two big digits.
Writes the four characters of one two-by-two digit (digit in A, column in Y) into the panel screen.
The message numbers of the sub-menu verbs (HIDE is the first and needs none; then INPUT, DESCRIBE) as the utilise menu cycles.
Three words (address minus one) of the starting routines of the HIDE, INPUT and DESCRIBE sub-modes.
Data at $1665 (f_1665): read by mode_utilise_menu.

Handler for the UTILISE action (entry 3 of the table at $0675). With nothing queued it queues UTILISE, then NOTHING TO USE when Johnny holds nothing (message 15), else it shows FIRE TO with HIDE and enters mode 5.
Mode 5: a direction press steps through HIDE, INPUT, DESCRIBE (queueing each verb) and wraps to ABORT; fire jumps through the table at $1664 to the setup of the chosen verb.
Mode 6: choose which held object to hide: a direction press moves to the next one, fire selects it and moves to mode 7.

Mode 7: after a delay of 100 passes it checks that the container at this column is unlocked and not full, then moves the chosen object from the inventory into the room's object table at the player's column and layer.
Mode 10: choose which held object to INPUT: a direction press moves to the next, fire selects it (kept in $02FF) and moves to mode 11.
Mode 11: after a delay of 100 passes it looks the player's column up in the terminal table at $15CC and jumps to that terminal's handler, or says NO EFFECT.
Mode 8: choose which held object to DESCRIBE; fire selects and moves to mode 9.
Mode 9: after a delay of 100 passes it queues the description text of the chosen object (description index plus 75) and returns to mode 0.

Handler for the LASER action. If a LASER ROM (object 0) is in the inventory it returns at once, leaving the laser to the part-two code; without it, and with nothing queued, it queues MALFUNCTION and NEED MORE INPUT and the prompt.

Handler for the JUMP action. Without a JUMP ROM (object 2) in the inventory it queues MALFUNCTION and NEED MORE INPUT; with one, and no jump already under way, it starts a jump: it records Johnny's sprite 1 height and the stick, and begins the arc at $19A5.
Runs once a pass: while a jump is active it replays the stick direction held at take-off and moves both player sprites up, then down, by the values in the arc table at $19CA.
Fifteen vertical steps (rise then fall) of a jump, added to or subtracted from the player sprites' Y.
Tests one key of the keyboard matrix. A is the key number (row times 8 plus column); returns carry set when it is held. Keeps the CIA ports restored afterwards.
The eight CIA1 port A values that select one keyboard column at a time.
Sixteen entries indexed by the inverted stick bits; the low bits hold the direction number 0 to 10, and $FF marks impossible combinations such as left plus right.
Mode 0, walking: moves Johnny by the stick, changing his walk frame when the direction changes, and works the walk cycle and scroll start.
Writes the pair of sprite pointers of walk frame X into $C3F8 and $C3F9.
Sets the walk animation tick counter $0298 to 3.
Advances Johnny's walk animation unless the walk flag is set.
Selects the frame table for direction Y and starts it.
Writes the current pair of sprite pointers of the frame table to $C3F8 and $C3F9.
Looks up the map character one cell ahead of Johnny's feet and stops him when it is a wall (character $76 twice in a row), and after that tests sprite overlaps against sprite 2.
Pairs of X and Y offsets, one pair for each of the eight directions, that place the feet probe relative to the sprite.
Data at $1BC2 (f_1BC2): read by walk_collision_check.
Tests whether the enemy sprites are near Johnny's sprite pair and whether the sprites are enabled, to decide whether he is stopped.
Returns the difference between the Y positions of sprite 2 and sprite 0.
Eight words (address minus one) of the walk steps, indexed by direction: up, down, left, right and the diagonals use $05D0, $05F8, $0613 and $063A.
Data at $1C2F (f_1C2F): read by sprite_height_difference.

Johnny's walk frame data: direction codes ($1C42), pointers to the frame tables ($1C4C, $1C60) and the sprite pointer pairs of each frame ($1C60 onwards) that $1AF0 and $1B51 write into the sprite pointers at $C3F8.
Data at $1C4C (f_1C4C): read by set_frame_table.
Data at $1C4D (f_1C4D): read by set_frame_table.
Data at $1C60 (f_1C60): read by set_walk_frame_pointers, enemy_walk.
Data at $1C61 (f_1C61): read by set_walk_frame_pointers, enemy_walk.
Data at $1C7A (f_1C7A): read by overlay_actor_update.
Data at $1C86 (f_1C86): read by actor_0231_update, move_pair_b5.
Scrolls the message window up by one line: copies each of the four text rows up and blanks the last.
INPUT handler for a container with a key lock: sets the object numbers that open it and the messages to show, then goes to the shared check at $1CFA.

Shared lock check: finds the container at the player's column in $15BC; the right key object opens it (sets its bit in $020B, adds a score bonus and queues the opened message), a repeat says it is already open, and the other key jams it.

INPUT handler for the first terminal column: the PASSCARD (object 14) gives SECURITY CLEARANCE GIVEN and sets $0210 to $11; any other object sets the alarm flag $0211, queues ALARM HAS GONE OFF and, when the decoy has not been built, sets $0219 to 1.

INPUT handler of the computer terminal columns: the object number picks the step - PASSWORD logs on, COMPUTER PROTOCOLS links up, SECURITY DOCUMENT toggles the alarm override, FIRE SYSTEM MANUAL toggles the sprinkler system.
Copies the status panel's characters from $9100 and $91B4 into the panel screen at $C258 and $C30C and draws the score and clock.

Fills the colour map from a block of screen characters through the table at $9000 (the character colours), reading each character with the undocumented opcode LAX; part of the picture and panel drawing.
Drains the energy bar by one step: increments the character in the bar's cell and rolls to the next cell, setting the out-of-energy flag at $0206 when the bar is empty.
The same drain for the second bar (the one labelled S), at $029B.

Called once a pass while the alarm flag $0211 is clear: when the clock's minutes digit is zero (each ten minutes) and the byte at $15B8 is not $0D it queues message 32 and jumps to the alarm path at $1DAC.
Reads the CIA1 time-of-day tenths register, which also releases the clock latch.
Compares the player's column with $63: crossing it sets or clears a flag in $0210; on a first crossing with the right flag it jumps to $1DAC.
If the player's column is at or beyond $95 and bit 2 of $0299 is set, it jumps to $1DAC.
Awards 5000 points and sets a flag the first time the object at $15A8 is gone from the table.
Counts minutes after the flag is set and starts the sequence at $0219 after four.
Fires the end-of-game routine at $225E when the timer reaches zero.
Converts a decimal digit in A into the panel character for it.
Runs the enemy walk step twice.
Moves the enemy robot pair (sprites 2 and 3) towards Johnny's height, with a small state machine in $0213 to $0216 for each step.
Sets the enemy step timer $0216 to 6.
Switches the enemy sprites on or off at a map column listed in $21CB when Johnny's scroll position matches.
The four scroll columns at which the enemy robot pair is switched on or off by $216F.

Polls the F7 key (key 3 of the matrix). While it is first pressed it freezes the time-of-day clock (reading and rewriting the hours register holds the clock) and waits in a loop for a second F7 press, then restores the tenths-of-seconds register to restart the clock and sets $0306 to 1.

End-of-part-one check made when the player walks into the exit area: needs four objects in the inventory; each of the four listed at $225A found adds 2000 points; if the hold is not full or any is missing it queues two messages (MALFUNCTION and MORE INPUT NEEDED FOR SURVIVAL) and returns with carry set.
The four object numbers needed to build the decoy robot at the end of part one.
Waits in a busy loop (about 0.04 s per pass) draining the energy bar and the shield bar one step each until the out-of-energy flag at $0206 is set. Used by the failure endings.

Once per pass when the alarm state at $0219 is nonzero: decides from sprite 2's position whether the guard comes from the right (state 1) or the left (state 2), then every second pass calls the matching mover ($22D0 or $2333).
Brings on sprites 4 and 5 (a guard and its shadow) at the right and walks them left towards Johnny; when they overlap Johnny they trigger the capture ending.
The same for sprites 6 and 7, which walk in from the left.
Queues the CAPTURED AND DEACTIVATED message and runs the energy drain loop to the end.
Moves sprites 4 and 5 two pixels left, flipping between walk frames from the table at $23F8.
Moves sprites 6 and 7 two pixels right, flipping between walk frames from the table at $23FC.
Two four-frame cycles of sprite pointers: $F1 to $F4 for the guard walking left, $E2 to $E5 for the guard walking right.
Data at $23FC (f_23FC): read by guard_left_animate, move_actor_pair.

Waits for the message queue to empty, zeroes the game's variables from $0200 to $0294, copies 13 start values from $2602 into $0295 onwards and refills the object table at $1568 from the 21 start columns at $260F, each set to layer 3.
When the scroll column is between $EC and $FB it tests the clock minutes; most of the time it sets the alarm state to 2, otherwise it awards 2000 points once.
Copies two blocks of 240 bytes from $9268 and $9358 into the screen and colour maps and runs the picture expander at $1EC6, with the VIC set to screen 4 while it does so.
Copies 16 bytes of start positions to the sprite registers, eight sprite pointers to $C3F8 and eight colours to $D027.
Sixteen start values for the sprite position registers ($24B9) followed by eight sprite pointers ($24C9) and eight sprite colours ($24D1) that $2498 loads.
Data at $24C9 (f_24C9): read by init_sprites.
Data at $24D1 (f_24D1): read by init_sprites.

Reads the time-of-day clock. At hour 3 with minutes below $30 it enables sprites 0 to 3 and 6 and 7 and returns carry clear; otherwise it leaves only sprites 6 and 7 on and returns carry set, meaning the thirty minutes are up.
End-of-part-one scene: waits on frame flag $02BE and walks sprites 6 and 7 to the left, changing frame every four pixels, and then moves sprite 0 and 2 to 7 left.
Gives 2000 points the first time the player's map column is between $3D and $FB.
Called when part one is won: adds 10000 points, then a bonus for the minutes and the seconds left, plays the walk-off scene and resets the game state.
Waits until the frame counter $0306 reaches $F0, then calls $AC8D until it returns zero, and clears the counter.
Thirteen start values for the variables from $0295 ($2602), then the 21 start columns of the objects ($260F) that $2400 loads.
Data at $260F (f_260F): read by reset_game_state.

Entry of part two: clears the state, sets sprite colours, positions the player and the lorry, resets the clock to 6:00, draws the panel, programs CIA2 timer A, shows the PART TWO text and falls into the part-two main loop.
Main loop of part two: handles the energy-out ending, then waits for the frame counter, and each frame runs the scroller, the character, the objects and the obstacles in turn.
Frame tail of part two: runs the animators, the sound driver call at $8930 and the message printer.
Installs part two's interrupt set-up: disables the CIA1 interrupts, enables the raster interrupt, selects screen 1 and sets the IRQ vector to $27A1 and the NMI vector to $2956.

Part two's raster handler. Saves the registers, acknowledges the VIC, steps the band counter at $02 through 2, 1, 0 and dispatches by RTS through the three-entry table at $27C8 to the handler for the band.
Three words (address minus one) of the part-two raster handlers: $27CE, $2804, $282E, indexed by the band counter.
Data at $27C9 (f_27C9): read by part_two_irq.

Part two's raster handler for line $61: sets the lower playfield band's screen from $029E and scroll from $02A0 with the colours $09 and $05, shifts the rows once if $0247 is set, and sets the next interrupt line to $A3.
Restores A, X and Y and returns from the part-two raster interrupt.

Part two's raster handler for the band at line $A3: selects the panel's screen and colours with the fixed scroll $18, counts the frame counter $0306 up, runs a scroll step if $21 asks for one, and sets the next interrupt line to $F3.

Part two's raster handler for line $F3: sets the upper playfield band's screen (0), scroll ($029F) and colours for the next frame, runs the sound timer, updates the clock and sets the next interrupt line to $61.
Part of the part-two scroll: moves the sprite slots one pixel and starts a new scroll step.
Frees sprite slot X when its ninth X bit is clear, or clears the bit.
Moves the active sprite slots one pixel to the left with the scroll, and at the end of each character shifts the eight rows of the screen map and colour map one place to the left.

Called from the NMI: advances the scroll position by one pixel step (phase $02AD, column $02AE) and, each time the phase wraps, draws the next 4-by-4 tile column of the scenery into the screen and colour maps through the row pointers in zero page $10 and $30, taking the tile numbers from the map rows at $4400 and $4500.
Writes one tile column (tile number in A) of part two's scenery: for each of the characters of the tile it stores the character and its colour (from $9448) through the row pointer tables.
Converts a tile number in A to its character data address, $4600 plus 16 times the number, in zero page $24 and $25.

Non-maskable interrupt handler of part two, driven by CIA2 timer A. If the serial-port bit is set it goes to $2B25; otherwise on a timer underflow it re-arms the timer, enables interrupts, shifts seven rows of the colour map one cell left and calls $28EC for the new column.
Shifts eight rows of the part-two screen and colour maps one character to the left, wrapping the first column to the end, to scroll the lower band of the picture by a character.

Builds part two's whole starting scenery: expands ten tile columns of two rows of tiles each from the map rows at $2B21 into the screen map at $C0F0 and then copies the screen and colour maps for the lower rows from the tile data.

Fills part two's colour map at $D850 and $D8F0 from the characters on screen, looking each one up in the colour tables at $4320 (characters $80 up) and $9448, reading each character with the undocumented opcode LAX.
Copies the two 16-byte tables of row pointers from $5BD0 and $5BE0 into zero page $10 to $1F and $30 to $3F.
Two pointers, to the map rows at $4400 and $4500, used by $2A42.
Data at $2B22 (f_2B22): read by draw_part_two_screen.
Handles the CIA2 serial-port NMI source: re-programs timer A with a short count, waits a short loop, restores the serial data register and jumps to $0107.
Copies 160 bytes of screen data from $4300 into the top of the screen map at $C050.
Fills four 256-byte blocks of the screen map ($C000, $C100, $C200, $C2E8) with the blank character $F8.
Reads the joystick on CIA1 port A, inverts the five bits, and looks the result up in the table at $1A1B to get the direction in zero page $20 (a negative table entry gives 0).
Part two's player movement: continues a started walk step, or reads the stick and starts a new one, selecting the movement routine from the table at $8FE8 by the stick bits.

Part two's action for the stick pushed up: unless the sprite slots are already on a path ($026B), it starts slots 0 and 1 on the jump path and sets the jump frames: sprite pointers $A0 and $A1 when Johnny faces right ($0297 is 7), otherwise $A2 and $A3.
Part two's action for the stick pushed down: clears the walking flag, sets the duck frame choice from $0303, and falls into the duck step at $2C38.
Part-two duck: counts the duck timer $029D down, sets the duck sprite frame and starts the ducking animation; at zero it ends the duck.
Part two's action for the stick pushed left: if the walking flag $02ED is set, takes a left step ($2C81) and advances the walk frame.
Moves the player's two sprites one pixel left, down to X $40, or ends the walk at the limit.
Part two's action for the stick pushed right: if the walking flag $02ED is set, takes a right step ($2CA4) and advances the walk frame with the table at $0E.
Moves the player's two sprites one pixel right, up to X $B0, once per call.
Part two's stick action for up and left: turns Johnny to face left if he is not, otherwise runs the jump start and the left walk.
Part two's stick action for down and left: turns Johnny to face left, then runs the duck step and the left walk.
Part two's stick action for up and right: turns Johnny to face right, then runs the jump start and the right walk.
Part two's stick action for down and right: turns Johnny to face right, then runs the duck step and the right walk.
Marks Y consecutive entries of the eight-slot shot tables, starting at X, as active and moving up.

Moves each active entry of the eight-slot table at $026B along a path read from $8FC8, advancing a step counter in $027B and switching direction in $0273 at step $20; an entry that has stepped back to zero is released.
Chooses the second sprite's pointer from the table at $2DBE (the walk or the duck frame, by the animation phase) and writes it to $C3F9.
Sprite pointers of the player's second sprite for the walk and duck frames, indexed by the animation phase.
Event routine: allocates a sprite for the entity in slot $0222 and colours it.
Per-pass routine of the entity whose slot is in $0222: moves it left, on reaching the edge of the screen frees it and awards points, and when it overlaps the player's sprite it hurts the player.
Event 4: allocates a sprite at the right edge at height $98 for the entity in slot $0223 and colours it 8.
Per-pass routine of the entity whose slot is in $0223: moves it right, awards points on leaving the screen, and hurts the player on contact at the right height.
Event 2: allocates a sprite at the right edge at height $8A for the entity in slot $0225 and colours it 1.
Per-pass routine of the entity in slot $0225: moves it, awards a point on leaving and tests contact with the player.
Event 7: allocates a sprite at the right edge at height $8D for the pair in slots $0227 and $0228 and colours it 7.
Per-pass routine of the entity pair in $0227 and $0228: spawns its second sprite when the first has crossed a column, moves both, awards points when they leave and hurts the player on contact.
Event 6: allocates a sprite at the right edge at height $8C for the entity in slot $0229, sets $0234 to 1 and colours it 9.
Per-pass routine of the entities in slots $0229 and $022A: spawns the second, moves both, tests for the player and awards points at column $A2.
Moves the entity in X by one pixel step, left or right according to flag $0234.
Spawns the first two members of a group.
Per-pass routine of the group of five entities from $022B: spawns them in a row and moves each, setting their sprite frames from the table at $8FAF.
Allocates a sprite for one member of the group, gives it its colour and its sprite pointer, and records its slot.
Spawns the group's members, one after another, once the first has crossed column $9C.
The sprite pointers $8B, $8A, $8C of the group.
Sprite pointers ($30BE) and Y positions ($30C1) of the members of the group spawned by $30A9.
Data at $30C1 (f_30C1): read by spawn_group_member.
Event routine: starts the entity in slot $0230, its sprite pair and colour.
Per-pass routine of the entity in slot $0230 (the one the player can shoot): moves it, tests for contact with the player or the lorry and awards points when it is shot.
Moves an entity and its shadow sprite one step left, or right, together.
Starts a pair of entities that chase the player: allocates sprites on the left and right edges once, and sets their colour and pointer.
Per-pass routine of the chasing entity in slot $0232: moves it, and when it is far enough from the player starts the next one at $32DA.
Allocates a sprite pair for the entity in $0231 and sets its colour and pointers.
Per-pass routine of the entity in slot $0231: moves it and drains the player's energy by 24 steps when it touches.
Moves sprite slot X and the slot after it one pixel to the right, then jumps to $323E to set the second sprite's frame pointer.
Moves a sprite pair one step left, setting the first sprite pointer to $B5.
Allocates a sprite for the entity in $0233 and gives it the position of the entity in $0230.
Per-pass routine of the entity in slot $0233: moves it, and when it has passed the player's sprite drains the energy or shield.
Plays the hit sound ($9B3F), then drains the player's energy bar by Y steps when carry is clear, or the shield bar when carry is set.
Frees sprite slot X, then drains the energy or shield as $32C7 does, by Y steps.
Allocates a sprite for the entity in $0235 and gives it the position of the entity in $0232.
Per-pass routine of the entity in slot $0235: moves it, and when it passes the player's sprite drains the energy by 24 steps.
Allocates two sprites and starts the overlay sprite pair at $0293.
Per-pass routine of the overlay pair started by $332F.
Allocates a sprite for the entity in slot $0236 at the height in $0256 and gives it a path.
Per-pass routine of the entity in slot $0236: moves it and drains the player when it passes.
Event 5: allocates a sprite at the left edge at height $7B for the entity in slot $023A and colours it 3.
Per-pass routine of the entity in slot $023A.
Event 11: allocates a sprite at the right edge at height $6A for the entity in slot $023D and colours it 1.
Per-pass routine of the entity pair in $023D and $023E: spawns the second on column $9C, moves both, and hurts the player on overlap.
Event 3: allocates a sprite at the right edge at height $94 for the entity in slot $0226 and colours it 8.
Per-pass routine of the entity in slot $0226: moves it, awards points on leaving, and hurts the player on contact.
Event 12: allocates a sprite at the left edge at height $8C for the entity in slot $023F and colours it 14.
Per-pass routine of the entity in slot $023F: moves it and hurts the player on contact.
Event 13: allocates a sprite at the left edge at height $8C for the entity in slot $0240 and colours it 3.
Per-pass routine of the entity in slot $0240: moves it and hurts the player on contact.
